intro: Wrestling may be the oldest sport people still practice. Painters in Egypt put wrestlers on tomb walls about 4,000 years ago. Greek boys trained for it in sandy yards. Mongolia, Turkey, India and Switzerland each have their own old styles.

Leagues, clocks and weight classes came much later. The modern Olympics added weight classes in 1904. In Illinois, the state high school association named its first wrestling champions in 1937. Girls got their own Illinois state finals in 2022.

In this unit, you will read paintings, stories, programs and laws. You can tell a record from a legend. You can explain why a first championship is a start line for a record, not the birthday of a sport.
bigQuestion: If wrestling is thousands of years old, what really began when leagues and schools wrote it down?

title: Wrestling Older Than the League

chapters.title: Holds Before Stadiums
chapters.bigQuestion: How do we know people wrestled long before there were leagues, clocks and weight classes?

story.title: Stone Wrestlers in Athens
story.kicker: A carved stone in a museum is far older than any gym clock.
paragraphs: In Athens, Greece, a block of white marble sits in the National Archaeological Museum. It was carved around 510 BCE. That is about 2,500 years ago. Once it held up a statue over a grave.
In 1922, workers found the block inside an old city wall of Athens. People long ago had reused it as a building stone. The wall kept its carvings safe for many centuries.
One side of the block shows young athletes. In the middle, two wrestlers face each other. A young man stands at each side and watches. The carver cut every arm and leg with care.
The scene has no clock on the wall. It has no scale for weighing people. It has no league name and no printed bracket. Those things came much later, over the last two hundred years.

Stones like this one help historians. They show that wrestling is very old. They also show that its rooms and rules have changed many times. Other old pictures and figures of wrestlers survive from Egypt, Mesopotamia and China.
story.think: What can a carving tell us about a sport, and what can it not tell us?

lessons.title: The Walls of Beni Hasan
lessons.mainIdea: Tomb paintings at Beni Hasan in Egypt show hundreds of pairs of wrestlers from about 4,000 years ago.
reading: Beni Hasan is a place on the east bank of the Nile River in Egypt. Local leaders were buried there in tombs cut into a cliff. Many of these tombs date to Egypt's *Middle Kingdom*. That time lasted from about 2000 to 1700 BCE.

Painters covered the tomb walls with scenes of life. Some walls show wrestlers in long rows. There are hundreds of pairs in all. Each pair is painted in a different position, one after another, like frames in a comic strip.

These paintings are *primary sources*. A primary source is something made at the time being studied. The Beni Hasan walls prove that Egyptians knew wrestling well. They do not tell us the rules the wrestlers followed.

words.d: a time in ancient Egypt, about 2000 to 1700 BCE
things made at the time being studied, like paintings, letters or programs
a room or grave where a person is buried

look.title: Rows on a Tomb Wall
look.text: Picture a long wall inside a cliff tomb in Egypt. Row after row of painted pairs stretch across it. Each pair is a little different from the one before. Some men are painted in darker colors and some in lighter colors, so you can tell the two apart.
look.prompt: Why might a painter make two wrestlers different colors?

lessons.title: A Story From Mesopotamia
lessons.mainIdea: The Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the oldest written stories, tells of two heroes who wrestle and then become friends.
reading: *Mesopotamia* is the old name for the land between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers. Today most of it is in Iraq. People there wrote on clay tablets. They pressed marks into wet clay with a reed.

One famous story from there is the *Epic of Gilgamesh*. Gilgamesh was a king of the city of Uruk. In the story, he meets a wild man named Enkidu. The two wrestle in a doorway. After the match, they become best friends.

The Epic is a story, not a sports report. We cannot tell whether the match happened. Still, it shows that wrestling mattered to its writers. Many copies were found in the ruins of Nineveh, in a library of King Ashurbanipal.

words.d: the old name for the land between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers, mostly in Iraq today
a very old story from Mesopotamia about King Gilgamesh of Uruk

lessons.title: The Palaestra and Olympia
lessons.mainIdea: Greek boys trained in a building called a palaestra, and wrestling joined the Olympic Games in 708 BCE, by ancient count.
reading: In ancient Greece, many cities had a *palaestra*. It was a building with an open, sandy yard in the middle. Rooms for washing and oiling the body lined the sides. Boys and young men trained there with a teacher.

The Olympic Games were held at Olympia every four years. Ancient writers said they began in 776 BCE with one footrace. Wrestling was added in 708 BCE, by the same ancient count. It was the first contest there that was not a race.

The Greek word for wrestling was *pale*. The name palaestra comes from it. At Olympia, only free Greek men and boys could compete. Enslaved people could not enter. Married women were not allowed to watch.

lessons.title: Milo and the Missing Clock
lessons.mainIdea: Milo of Croton won Olympic wrestling six times, in a sport with no weight classes and no time limit.
reading: *Milo of Croton* is the most famous wrestler of ancient Greece. Croton was a Greek city in southern Italy. Milo lived in the 500s BCE. Ancient writers say he won at Olympia six times, once as a boy.

Greek wrestling had no *weight classes*. A weight class is a group of people close in body weight. At Olympia, a small man could be matched with a very big one. Big, strong men often won for that reason.

Greek wrestling also had no clock. Ancient writers say a wrestler needed three falls to win. A match lasted until that happened. Later tales made Milo seem larger than life. Historians treat those tales as legends.

lessons.title: Bökh at Naadam
lessons.mainIdea: In Mongolia, wrestling called bökh is one of the three games of the Naadam festival each July.
reading: In *Mongolia*, wrestling is called *bökh*. It is one of the country's best-loved sports. It is part of the big summer festival called *Naadam*. The national Naadam opens in the capital, Ulaanbaatar, on July 11.

Naadam has three main games: wrestling, horse racing and archery. People often call them the three games of men. Today women and girls compete in the archery and girls ride in the horse races. Wrestling at Naadam is for men.

Bökh has no weight classes. Winners earn titles, such as Falcon, Elephant, Lion and Titan. A story says the wrestling jacket is open at the chest because a woman once won in disguise. That story is a legend. In 2010, UNESCO listed Naadam as world heritage.

lessons.title: Oil Wrestling at Kırkpınar
lessons.mainIdea: Turkey's Kırkpınar oil wrestling festival, near Edirne, is held every summer and traces its start to the 1300s.
reading: In Turkey, one old style is *oil wrestling*. Wrestlers cover their bodies with olive oil before a match. They wear heavy leather trousers called *kispet*. The oil makes the match slippery.

The most famous oil wrestling festival is *Kırkpınar*. It is held each summer near the city of Edirne, in northwest Turkey. Its organizers say it began in the 1300s, in the time of the Ottoman Empire. That start date comes from tradition.

The winner at Kırkpınar is named başpehlivan, which means chief wrestler. A gold belt goes to the champion. In 2010, UNESCO listed the Kırkpınar festival as world heritage. The same year, it listed Mongolia's Naadam.

words.d: a Turkish style in which wrestlers cover themselves with olive oil
heavy leather trousers worn in Turkish oil wrestling

lessons.title: The Akhara in India
lessons.mainIdea: In India and Pakistan, kushti wrestlers train in an akhara, a pit of soft earth led by a teacher called a guru.
reading: In India and Pakistan, an old style of wrestling is called *kushti*. Another name is pehlwani. A wrestler is called a pehlwan. The style grew from older Indian wrestling mixed with Persian wrestling.
Kushti wrestlers train in an *akhara*. An akhara is a training place with a pit of soft, dug earth. Wrestlers often live and eat together there. A teacher, called a *guru*, leads the akhara.

Many akharas still run today, in cities like Varanasi. Kushti wrestlers also moved onto modern mats. In 1952, K. D. Jadhav won a wrestling bronze at the Helsinki Olympics. It was independent India's first Olympic medal won by one person.

a kushti training place with a pit of soft earth

lessons.title: Schwingen in Switzerland
lessons.mainIdea: Swiss wrestling, called Schwingen, takes place in a ring of sawdust, and its big national festival crowns a king.
reading: In Switzerland, the old national style of wrestling is called *Schwingen*. It grew among farmers and herders in the Alps. Wrestlers meet in a round ring covered with *sawdust*. The sawdust makes a soft floor outdoors.

Swiss wrestlers wear short trousers made of tough cloth over their clothes. The trousers have a belt. The match is decided inside the sawdust ring. The loser often brushes the sawdust off the winner's back.

The biggest Schwingen event is a national festival held every three years. Its champion earns the title of Schwingerkönig, which means wrestling king. By tradition, the king wins a live bull as a prize.

lessons.title: Weight Classes Come to the Olympics
lessons.mainIdea: The modern Olympics had one open wrestling event in 1896, added weight classes in 1904, and added women in 2004.
reading: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896. They had one wrestling event, in *Greco-Roman* style. It had no weight classes. Carl Schuhmann of Germany won it. He also won medals in gymnastics.

In 1904, the Olympics came to St. Louis, Missouri. That year, *freestyle* wrestling joined the Games. It was split into weight classes. All the wrestlers were from the United States. After that, weight classes became normal in Olympic wrestling.

In 1912, national wrestling groups formed a world *federation*. Today it is called United World Wrestling. It writes the rules for Olympic wrestling. Women's wrestling first came to the Olympics in Athens in 2004.

words.d: a modern Olympic wrestling style, named in honor of ancient Greece and Rome
a modern Olympic wrestling style, first in the Olympics in 1904

lessons.title: The School Match Clock
lessons.mainIdea: School and college wrestling in the United States runs on a clock, with periods and weight classes set by rule books.
reading: In the United States, school wrestling has its own style. People call it *folkstyle*, or scholastic wrestling. It is different from the Olympic styles. American high schools and colleges use it.

High schools follow rules from the *NFHS*. That stands for the National Federation of State High School Associations. It began in 1920 at a meeting in Chicago. Its rules set three periods of two minutes each. They also set 14 weight classes.

Colleges follow a separate NCAA rule book. A college match has a longer first period, so it runs seven minutes. The first NCAA wrestling championship was held in 1928. The clock, the scale and the bracket are the newest parts of a very old sport.

chapters.title: Illinois 1937
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the year 1937 mark in Illinois wrestling, and what does it not mark?

story.title: Names Under a State Seal
story.kicker: An old program shows the first year Illinois named high school wrestling champions.
paragraphs: Picture a student in an Illinois library. She opens a folder of old papers. Inside is a thin program from 1937. At the top are a state seal and the name of the state's high school association.
Below the seal are lists. Each list has a weight at the top. Under each weight are names of boys and the high schools they came from. The paper is yellow and soft at the edges.
In 1937, the association named its first state champions in wrestling. One boy won in each weight class. His name went into the state record. That record has grown every winter since.

The student looks at the date again. Wrestling in Illinois did not begin that year. Abraham Lincoln wrestled at New Salem more than a hundred years earlier. Paid wrestlers filled Chicago arenas before 1937 too.
So what began in 1937? A school contest began, with a state seal, a scale and a written list. The program marks the start of a record, not the start of a sport.
story.think: Why might the first year of a state title be a different date from the first year of a sport?

sections.title: The Body That Runs School Sports

lessons.title: An Association Since 1900
lessons.mainIdea: The Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, is the group of member schools that runs state contests in Illinois.
reading: In the late 1800s, students often ran their own school teams. They set their own schedules. Some players were not even students. School leaders wanted fair, shared rules for every team.

In 1900, Illinois schools formed a state *association*. An association is a group that joins together under one set of rules. Today it is called the *IHSA*, the Illinois High School Association. Its main office is in Bloomington, Illinois.

High schools choose to become *member schools* of the IHSA. They agree to follow its rules. The IHSA decides who may play, and it runs the state series. A state series is the set of contests that ends with state champions.

words.d: a group that joins together under one set of rules
the Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, which runs high school state contests
schools that join an association and agree to follow its rules

look.title: Before and After an Association
look.text: Before: each school team makes its own rules. One team lets older men play. Another does not. After: every member school signs on to one rule book. Every team knows who may play and how the champion is chosen.

lessons.title: The Rule Book and the Scale
lessons.mainIdea: Illinois high school wrestling follows the NFHS rule book, which sets weight classes and a weigh-in before each meet.
reading: State associations share one national rule book for each high school sport. The *NFHS* writes these books. It first met in Chicago in 1920. Illinois high schools follow its wrestling rules.
The rule book sets the *weight classes*. For boys, it lists 14 classes. They run from 106 pounds up to 285 pounds. Each wrestler meets only people in the same class.
Before each meet, wrestlers step on a scale. This is called the *weigh-in*. It shows which class each wrestler may enter. The rule book is updated often, so rules can change from year to year.

lessons.title: Champions by Weight, 1937
lessons.mainIdea: In 1937, the IHSA named its first boys' state wrestling champions, one in each weight class.
reading: The IHSA crowned its first state champions in boys' wrestling in 1937. That was 37 years after the association began. By then, the IHSA already ran state contests in other sports, such as basketball and track.

A wrestling state final is a *tournament*. A tournament is a contest with many matches that ends with one winner. Wrestlers are placed in a *bracket*. A bracket is a chart that shows who meets whom in each round.
Each weight class has its own bracket. So a state final names many champions, not just one. Teams earn points from their wrestlers' wins. Each champion's name joins the IHSA's written record.

words.d: a contest with many matches that ends with one winner
a chart that shows who meets whom in each round of a tournament

lessons.title: Reading an Old Program
lessons.mainIdea: An old meet program is a primary source that can show names, schools and weights, but not everything that happened.
reading: A *program* is a printed paper handed out at an event. A wrestling program lists the weight classes. It lists the wrestlers and their schools. It may show the date, the place and the seal of the association.
A program from 1937 is a *primary source*. It was made at the time being studied. Historians use programs, newspapers and school yearbooks together. Each one can check the others.
A program also has limits. It is printed before the matches, so it cannot tell who won. It may leave out people who were not allowed to enter. Historians ask who is missing, as well as who is listed.

words.d: a printed paper handed out at an event, listing who takes part

lessons.title: A Start Line, Not a Birthday
lessons.mainIdea: The year 1937 marks the start of a school record in Illinois, not the invention of wrestling.
reading: People sometimes treat a first championship as the birthday of a sport. For wrestling, that would be a big mistake. Egyptian tomb paintings of wrestlers are about 4,000 years old. Greek wrestling joined the Olympic Games in 708 BCE.
What 1937 marks is a *record*. A record is a written list kept over time. The IHSA has kept its wrestling champions list every year since. The list lets people compare schools and years.
Many dates in school sports work this way. They mark when a body began counting. The NCAA held its first wrestling championship in 1928. The IHSA held its first girls' wrestling state finals in 2022.

words.d: a written list of results kept over time

lessons.title: Lincoln at New Salem
lessons.mainIdea: In 1831, young Abraham Lincoln wrestled Jack Armstrong at New Salem, Illinois, long before any school title.
reading: In 1831, Abraham Lincoln moved to *New Salem*, a small village on the Sangamon River in Illinois. He was about 22 years old. He worked as a clerk in a store owned by Denton Offutt.

Offutt bragged that Lincoln could beat any man around. A group of young men from nearby Clary's Grove took up the challenge. Their leader, Jack Armstrong, wrestled Lincoln. Old accounts disagree about who won, but they agree the two became friends.

William Herndon, Lincoln's law partner, told the story in his book, *Herndon's Lincoln*, in 1889. The match had no weight classes and no clock. Much later, the National Wrestling Hall of Fame honored Lincoln as an Outstanding American.

lessons.title: Frank Gotch in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1908 and 1911, Frank Gotch beat George Hackenschmidt in Chicago in famous professional matches.
reading: Frank Gotch was a farm boy from Humboldt, Iowa. He became a *professional* wrestler. A professional is paid to take part in a sport. In the early 1900s, pro wrestling matches drew big crowds and filled newspapers.

On April 3, 1908, Gotch met George Hackenschmidt in Chicago. Hackenschmidt was born in Estonia, then part of the Russian Empire. People called him the Russian Lion. Gotch won and became world heavyweight champion.

In 1911, they met again at Comiskey Park, the new home of the Chicago White Sox. A huge crowd came. Gotch won again. Later in the 1900s, pro wrestling turned into a planned show. School wrestlers stayed *amateurs*, who are not paid.

lessons.title: Title IX, 1972
lessons.mainIdea: Title IX, a 1972 law, says schools that get federal money cannot shut people out because of their sex.
reading: For most of the 1900s, school wrestling in Illinois was for boys. The 1937 program had only boys' names. Many schools had few sports of any kind for girls.

In 1972, Congress passed the Education Amendments. One part is called *Title IX*. President Richard Nixon signed it on June 23, 1972. It covers schools and colleges that get money from the *federal* government.

Title IX says those schools cannot leave people out because of their sex. Over time, schools added many girls' teams. For years, girls who wanted to wrestle joined the boys' team. Some of them were the only girl in the room.

words.d: a 1972 U.S. law that bans shutting people out of school programs because of sex

reading: As more girls joined wrestling, states began to hold separate girls' contests. Women's wrestling had joined the Olympics in Athens in 2004. That gave girls famous wrestlers to look up to.
In Illinois, the IHSA held its first *girls' state finals* in wrestling in 2022. That was during the 2021–22 school year. It came 85 years after the first boys' champions in 1937.

The first girls' champions started a new line in the IHSA record. Their weight classes are set for girls. From 2022 on, each year adds new names to both lists. Historians can now compare how the two lists grow.

lessons.title: A Champion Born With One Leg
lessons.mainIdea: Anthony Robles, born with one leg, won the NCAA wrestling title at 125 pounds in 2011.
reading: Anthony Robles was born in 1988 with only one leg. He grew up in Mesa, Arizona. He began wrestling as a young teenager. He used crutches to get around, not a prosthetic leg.

Robles wrestled in college for Arizona State University. In 2011, he won the *NCAA* championship at 125 pounds. He did not lose a match that whole season. The NCAA is the body that runs most college sports.

Robles showed that wrestling rooms can include many kinds of bodies. The weight class rule mattered here too. It matched him with people of the same weight. His story is told in his book, Unstoppable, published in 2012.
